display.purpose: Page-defining statements only. One per page at most; its authority comes from being alone.

headline.purpose: Section-leading statements and the hero sentence. Where the site speaks in its own voice.

title.purpose: Card and list-item titles, role names. The workhorse for anything scannable.

body.purpose: Prose and descriptions, constrained to ~42rem so lines never outrun the eye.

label.purpose: Machine truth: dates, content types, growth stages, project metadata. Uppercase and letterspaced.

shadows.name: artifact-rest
shadows.purpose: Interactive artifacts at rest in light mode. Barely there — enough to lift off the page.

shadows.name: artifact-hover
shadows.purpose: Light-mode hover lift on artifacts. Never on interface chrome.

shadows.name: dark-glow
shadows.purpose: The dark-mode counterpart to artifact-hover. Depth is emitted rather than cast.

motion.name: state-fast
motion.purpose: Default for color, border, and icon state changes. The most-used duration in the system.

motion.name: state-slow
motion.purpose: Button and card hover transitions, where a slower settle reads as considered.

motion.name: entrance
motion.purpose: Stagger-in on page load: opacity plus a 4px rise. Gated on html.js so content stays visible without JavaScript.

motion.name: ease-out-expo
motion.purpose: Artifact and lightbox motion. Fast departure, long settle.

motion.name: ease-overshoot
motion.purpose: Reserved for playful artifact motion only. Never for interface chrome.

components.name: Ghost Button
components.description: The only button variant. The system has no filled button, because a filled button would need a brand color it deliberately does not have.
components.html: About Me
components.css: .ds-btn-ghost { display: inline-flex; align-items: center; gap: 0.75rem; font-family: var(--font-mono, ui-monospace, monospace); font-size: 11px; text-transform: uppercase; letter-spacing: 0.12em; color: var(--color-text-secondary, #6b6b68); text-decoration: none; border: 1px solid var(--color-border, #ddd8d2); border-radius: 6px; padding: 0.375rem 0.875rem; transition: color 300ms ease, border-color 300ms ease; } .ds-btn-ghost svg { opacity: 0.4; } .ds-btn-ghost:hover { color: var(--color-text-primary, #1a1a18); border-color: var(--color-accent, #14100d); } .ds-btn-ghost:focus-visible { outline: 2px solid var(--color-accent, #14100d); outline-offset: 2px; }

components.name: Growth Badge
components.description: States the epistemic status of a piece of writing: seedling, growing, or evergreen. The clearest single-component expression of the workshop north star.
components.html: evergreen

components.name: Content Card
components.description: Case study and lab cards. Flat at rest; the border picks up the relevant accent on hover. The whole card is clickable via a stretched link, while the accessible name stays on the title.

A short description that explains what changed and for whom.

components.name: Empty Slot
components.description: The system's consistent signal for a real-but-unfilled slot: 1px dashed border, tonal fill, a pixel glyph, and a monospace hint naming what belongs there. Used by photo frames and draft sections.
components.css: .ds-slot { display: flex; flex-direction: column; align-items: center; justify-content: center; gap: 0.625rem; margin: 0; padding: 1rem; aspect-ratio: 1 / 1; text-align: center; border: 1px dashed var(--color-border, #ddd8d2); border-radius: 10px; background: color-mix(in srgb, var(--color-bg-secondary, #eae5df) 60%, transparent); color: var(--color-text-secondary, #6b6b68); } .ds-slot svg { opacity: 0.35; } .ds-slot-hint { font-family: var(--font-mono, ui-monospace, monospace); font-size: 11px; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 18rem; opacity: 0.75; }

components.name: Revising Statement
components.description: The homepage headline edits itself: the original phrase is struck through and a revision appears. Uses <del>/<ins>, so the revision is real semantics and the static state reads as an edited manuscript.
components.html: Alex is a designer who builds builder who designs
components.css: .ds-revise { font-family: var(--font-heading, serif); font-size: clamp(2rem, 5.5vw, 3.25rem); line-height: 1.15; letter-spacing: -0.01em; margin: 0; text-wrap: balance; } .ds-revise-was, .ds-revise-now { text-decoration: none; white-space: nowrap; } .ds-revise-was { position: relative; color: var(--color-text-secondary, #6b6b68); } .ds-revise-was::after { content: ""; position: absolute; left: -0.05em; right: -0.05em; top: 0.56em; height: 0.06em; background: currentColor; transform-origin: left center; } .ds-revise-now { color: var(--color-text-primary, #1a1a18); }

narrative.overview:
The site is the workshop, not the showroom. Tools stay visible, work sits on the bench in whatever state it is actually in, and nothing is staged for a photograph. This is why the experiments run live in the page instead of being screenshotted, why unfinished thinking carries a growth badge instead of being hidden until polished, and why metadata — dates, provenance, type — is exposed rather than tucked away. A showroom hides the process because the process is unflattering. A workshop shows it because the process is the evidence.

The system is quiet by construction. Warm near-black and warm near-white carry almost every surface; the type does the work; color is rationed so tightly that its appearance is meaningful. Dark is the default and the primary composition, not an inverted afterthought. Density is generous rather than tight — this is a place for reading and poking at things, not scanning a dashboard.

Three typefaces divide the labor cleanly and never trade jobs. A pixel display face carries voice, a neutral sans carries prose, and a monospace carries every piece of machine truth: dates, types, labels, counts. The monospace is the workshop's measuring tape — it appears wherever the system is stating a fact rather than making an argument.
keyCharacteristics: Warm neutral foundation (hue ~56) in both themes; never a cold or pure grey
Running prose is Inter at 15–17px; monospace is reserved for facts
Dark mode as the default composition, light as a true peer
Three fonts with strictly separated jobs — display, prose, machine truth
Color rationed to content-type identification; no decorative accents
Every animation degrades to fully visible content without JavaScript

rules.name: The Rationed Color Rule
rules.body: The three content accents identify content types and nothing else. They appear on type icons, hover states, and left-border accents. They never fill a button, never back a surface, never emphasize a word. On a typical page, colored pixels are well under 1% of the composition. That scarcity is the entire reason they read as a system rather than as decoration.

rules.name: The Warm Neutral Rule
rules.body: Every neutral sits at hue 34–58. There are no cold greys and no pure #000 or #fff anywhere in the system. If a new neutral is needed, it inherits the warmth or it does not belong.

rules.name: The Transparency-Over-Grey Rule
rules.body: Secondary text is the primary text color at reduced opacity, never a separately-chosen grey. It therefore adapts automatically to whatever surface it lands on, and can never drift out of key with its own theme.

rules.name: The Three Jobs Rule
rules.body: Mondwest speaks, Inter reads, JetBrains Mono states facts. A font never takes another's job. Prose never gets set in the display face because it looks characterful; a date never gets set in Inter because it fits better.

rules.name: The Monospace-Means-Fact Rule
rules.body: If it is machine truth — a date, a type, a duration, a count, a status, a file path — it is monospace, uppercase where it is a label, and letterspaced. If it is an argument, an opinion, or a description, it is not.

rules.name: The One Display Line Rule
rules.body: At most one Display-scale element per page. Its authority comes from being alone.

rules.name: The Column Rule
rules.body: Everything lives in the 56rem column. If a design idea requires breaking out of it, the idea changes, not the column.

rules.name: The Chrome-Is-Flat Rule
rules.body: If it is interface — nav, card, button, container, row — it has no shadow at rest. Depth in the interface layer comes from the background tonal step and hairline borders, never from elevation.

rules.name: The Glow-Inverts Rule
rules.body: In dark mode, depth is emitted rather than cast. A shadow that works on paper becomes a soft white glow on ink. Never ship a dark-mode surface with a black drop shadow; it is invisible and it reads as a bug.

rules.name: The Square-ish Rule
rules.body: Corners soften; they never round away. A 10px radius on a large card is the ceiling. Fully rounded containers belong to a different system.

rules.name: The No-Eyebrow Rule
rules.body: No kicker label above a heading. A section index that says "WORK" over a headline is repeating what the nav, the URL, and the title already said. The heading carries its own weight.

rules.name: The One Icon Family Rule
rules.body: Every icon comes from Lucide at 2px stroke. No mixed families, no one-off hand-drawn glyphs, no emoji standing in for an icon.

rules.name: The Two-Plane Card Rule
rules.body: A card carrying media has exactly two planes: media full-bleed to the edge, body padded beneath it. The card clips its own overflow so media meets the corner radius. Never pad the media.

dos: Do keep every neutral warm (hue 34–58) and every secondary text value a transparency of its primary, not a separate grey.
Do set machine truth in JetBrains Mono, uppercase and letterspaced when it functions as a label.
Do ship the live artifact when one is possible. A running prototype outranks an image of a running prototype, every time.
Do let the background tonal step and 1px hairlines carry separation in the interface layer.
Do invert depth to an emitted glow in dark mode.
Do gate every entrance animation on html.js so content stays visible without JavaScript, and honor prefers-reduced-motion.
Do use a dashed 1px border for any real-but-empty slot.
Do format every date in UTC. Frontmatter dates coerce to UTC midnight and shift a day without it — this has already been fixed once.
Do run card media full-bleed to the card edge and reserve padding for the body beneath it.
donts: Don't use the content accents for anything but content-type identification. No colored buttons, no colored backgrounds, no colored emphasis.
Don't introduce a brand hue. The absence of one is the position, not a gap.
Don't put a shadow on interface chrome, or a black drop shadow on a dark surface.
Don't set prose in PP Mondwest or metadata in Inter.
Don't exceed one Display-scale element per page.
Don't break content out of the 56rem column.
Don't add a raw hex value or a one-off font size. Tokens live in src/styles/global.css.
Don't fully round a container. 10px is the ceiling; pills are for badges and tooltips.
Don't compress the timeline rail on mobile — hide it. Narrow screens belong to content.
Don't set running prose in JetBrains Mono. Body copy is Inter; mono is for facts.
Don't put an eyebrow label above a heading.
Don't apply Tailwind Typography's prose classes to a bare inline link. It injects --tw-prose-links (a cold blue at hue 264) into a palette with no brand hue. Use .link-inline.
Don't mix icon families. Lucide at 2px stroke, or an official brand mark.
